sam_cs: FYI customer C-4821 hit a weird case: after a short network blip their client reconnected and we ended up with a partial chunk + a full retryed completion — they saw duplicate content and got billed twice. Raising since it's ambiguous if resume logic or client retry is at fault.

olivia_support: Ugh. Any chance they still have the client logs? What endpoint were they on (stream vs chunked SSE)?

sam_cs: They were using SSE /v1/streams/chat with resume tokens. Client log snippet attached by customer (redacted):

sam_cs: ```
EVENT: open
EVENT: message seq=12 resume_id=ka3l... chunk="Hello, wor"
EVENT: disconnect code=1006
EVENT: reconnect
EVENT: message seq=12 resume_id=ka3l... chunk="ld!
This is the rest."
EVENT: message seq=13 resume_id=ka3l... completion_id=cmpt-xyz content="Full response repeated"
```

michaela_eng: Hmm looks like they got seq=12 twice (partial then remainder) and then a full completion for the same logical request. Do they send an idempotency key / request id with the original open?

sam_cs: Customer claims they set an Idempotency header on the initial create and also passes session tokens for resume. Their code shows a naive retry: if websocket/SSE disconnect -> reconnect then re-POST if resume fails.

dylan_sre: Could be an ordering/race: server resumed and streamed the remainder, but the client timed out waiting for a final completion event and re-sent, which produced a new completion. Need to confirm server returned a resume-ack vs resume-miss. Any server logs for resume lookup?

michaela_eng: @dylan_sre, pulling logs now. If resume succeeded we should not accept a new create for same idempotency token within the same session window. But if the create was never tied to a persistent id (e.g., ephemeral session token rotated), dedupe might not match.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary inference-runtime v3.12.4 -> v3.12.5 scheduled at 03:00 UTC (changes include resume-window fix).

olivia_support: Customer also flagged billing — they saw two line items for the same interaction. Can finance confirm whether we billed per completion event or per token emitted?

sam_cs: FYI billing showed two charges: one small partial token charge and one larger final charge. They disputed the smaller one. Said they never consumed the partial message (client displayed only final).

michaela_eng: That aligns: tokens are metered per emitted token on the stream. So even partial fragments count. For usability we should consider emitting resume fragments with an "incomplete" flag that clients can introspect to decide dedupe/billing behavior, but that's product-level. For now, immediate mitigation: advise client to prefer server resume (do not auto-recreate request until resume window expires). Provide exact repro steps and a small client change we can recommend.

michaela_eng: Suggested messaging to customer: "On disconnect, first attempt to reconnect and supply your resume token. Only if the resume attempt fails (server returns resume_miss or you get no activity for X seconds) perform a new create with the same idempotency key. Avoid blind re-POSTs on short disconnects."

dylan_sre: Also add: on reconnect, compare the last-seen seq number. If you receive seq N then resume completed; do not re-POST. If you get duplicate seqs, client should de-duplicate by sequence id before re-displaying.

olivia_support: I'll send that recommendation. Also asking finance to put a temporary hold on dispute auto-accept for this account until CS escalates.

sam_cs: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate. Michaela, can you paste a minimal repro harness (curl + short node snippet) that demonstrates: quick disconnect -> resume success vs quick re-POST -> double completion?

michaela_eng: Sure, quick pseudo-repro (node):
```js
// open stream with resume_id and client_request_id header
fetch('/v1/streams/chat', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'req-123', 'Resume-Token': 'ka3l' } })
// simulate network blip: close socket after receiving first chunk
// reconnect and send resume token 
fetch('/v1/streams/reconnect?resume=ka3l')
// if client doesn't wait and instead POSTs same body: POST /v1/streams/chat { idempotency: 'req-123' } => server may create second completion if resume didn't bind
```

michaela_eng: I'll attach server-side query to check: search logs for resume_token=ka3l and idempotency=req-123 across the same session window. If both appear we can see whether resume was honored or new create accepted.

dylan_sre: Action items:
- olivia_support: communicate recommended client behavior + billing hold (ASAP)
- michaela_eng: collect resume_lookup logs + correlation id and escalate to infra/runtime team if resume lookup sometimes returns stale miss.
- sam_cs: ask customer to share raw SSE stream (not UI reassembled) and timestamps.

olivia_support: on it. I'll also ask for screenshot of billing lines and transaction ids.

sam_cs: Thanks all. One more thought: if we see this reproduce internally we should consider a server-side safety: ignore new create if a resume token within last 30s had an in-flight incomplete output for same idempotency — effectively prefer resume over new create for short windows. File a RFC?

michaela_eng: Agreed. If logs show racey behavior we'll propose that. Creating an internal bug now (BUG-11988) and linking thread. I'll post the logs here once I have them. :+1:
